text: The equivalence-principle calculation of light deflection by the Sun gives 2GM/(bc²), but the full GR result is twice as large, 4GM/(bc²). What accounts for the factor of 2?
choices: The equivalence principle is only an approximation that breaks down near massive bodies
Photons acquire an effective mass in a gravitational field that doubles the deflection
The full GR calculation adds the curvature of the spatial part of the metric to the temporal (time-dilation) part, and each contributes equally to the deflection of null geodesics
The equivalence-principle calculation neglects the cosmological constant Λ
explanation: The uniformly accelerated elevator (equivalence-principle) argument captures only the bending of the light ray's spatial path, giving 2GM/(bc²). In full GR the metric departs from flatness in both g_00 (gravitational time dilation) and the spatial g_rr, and these contribute equally to the bending of null geodesics, doubling the result to 4GM/(bc²), the value Eddington confirmed in 1919. Photons remain massless and Λ plays no role here.
